title: Works of mercy for the body
word: Works of mercy for the body
hookLine: feed, give drink, clothe, shelter, visit the sick and prisoners, bury the dead
tomorrow: works of mercy for the soul

cards: The table is set for a feast. A man named Tobit is about to eat, and he sends his son out to find a poor man to share the meal.
The son comes back with news instead: a man of their people has been killed, and his body is lying in the marketplace. Tobit gets up before he has tasted anything.
He carries the body to a room and waits for sunset to bury it. His neighbors laugh at him. Burying the dead has already got him into trouble with the king.
He does it anyway. His dinner, the book says, he ate in sorrow.

teach.b: Tobit's book sits in the Bibles of Catholic and Orthodox Christians; Protestant Bibles that print it place it among the books called the Apocrypha.

Either way, tradition says his story gave Christians one item on an old list: the works of mercy for the body. The rest comes straight from Jesus. In Matthew's Gospel he tells a story of the end of all things.

teach.h: I WAS AN HUNGRED, AND YE GAVE.
teach.b: The nations are gathered, and the king says to some of them: "For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me."
Add Tobit's burial to those, and that's the list the tradition hands on. Then the story turns.
The people the king praises don't know what he means: "Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee?" They never noticed. They were just feeding people.
And the king answers: "Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me." In this story, the hungry stranger and Christ are somehow the same face.
So these works aren't charity from a distance. They are hands: a plate, a cup, a coat, a chair beside a hospital bed, a visit through a glass window, a shovel at a grave.
Some Christians trace hospitals, soup kitchens and prison visiting back to these verses. But the works can stay small: one meal brought to one neighbor.

how: Christians practice the works of mercy for the body, often called the corporal works of mercy, through food banks, shelters, hospital and prison visiting, and funeral ministries, and in ordinary help to neighbors; the list comes from Matthew 25 with burial of the dead from Tobit.

games.q: what does “works of mercy for the body” mean?
o: healing miracles that only saints can perform
feeding, clothing, visiting, burying: care by hand
the rules for fasting and caring for your health

games.q: mercy with hands — tap the pairs.
p: left his feast to bury the dead
the surprise of the ones praised
ye have done it unto me

s: the people the king praises knew they were serving him
they ask, "Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee?" they never noticed.
burying the dead on the list comes from the book of Tobit
Tobit leaves his feast to bury a man left in the marketplace.
all Christian churches count Tobit as scripture
Catholic and Orthodox Bibles include it; Protestant churches usually place it in the Apocrypha.

games.q: you're Tobit. the feast is on the table, and your son says a man has been killed and left in the marketplace. burying the dead has already got you in trouble. what do you do?
o: eat first, and see to it in the morning.
get up before tasting anything and carry the body in.
send your son to tell the authorities.
games.why: he gets up before he has tasted the meal, brings the body in, and buries it after sunset, while his neighbors laugh at him.

practice: Let the king's list pass by slowly, the hungry, the thirsty, the cold, the homeless, the sick, the locked away, the grieving, until one face rises, and one small thing your hands could do for them: a meal, a call, a visit.
If you pray, you can hold that person before God.

orig.note: Greek: mercy, pity. The word in Matthew 9:13, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.
